newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME lumber futures close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME lumber futures close sharply higher.

text.p: Nearby CME lumber futures held sharp gains at the close as continued short covering and unwinding of bear spreads pushed prices higher, traders said.

Lack of carryover pressure after Monday's limit break sparked short covering from shortly after the start. Buy stops were hit during the day, adding to the advance which took November up to technical resistance, they said.

Although futures still look technically weak and cash lumber prices are expected to continue falling, futures are already at a sharp discount to cash and appeared oversold after Monday's limit break, they said.

Cash spruce is expected to be quoted in the $370 to $375 per tbf area Wednesday. Those values had fallen to $382 by last Friday, $50 under the recent high in the cash market. There is still no reason for buyers to step in as long as production outpaces demand, cash sources said.
Lumber closed $8.50 per tbf higher to $1.10 lower with November up most at $337.90 and January up $7.80 at $354.40 per tbf.
